Aljmas (port locode HRALJ) is a Danube River cruise port and village in Croatia's Osijek-Baranja County (eastern Slavonia) and part of the Erdut municipality, with a population of under 1,000. Erdut is located approx 37 km (23 mi) east of Osijek (on the Croatia-Serbia border). Aljmas is among the pilgrimage destinations in Croatia, being visited by around 100,000 tourists arriving here each year on August 15 to celebrate Virgin Mary's assumption into Heaven.

As a cruise port, Aljmas was added in the nickoVISION ship's 2019 schedule from homeport Passau.

At a Glance

Independent with some planning or transport. Aljmaš is a small Danube village rather than a conventional city port. Its church, riverfront and village streets are easily explored on foot, but the surrounding wineries, Erdut, Osijek and Kopački Rit Nature Park require arranged transport or an organized excursion.

Getting from the River Cruise Berth

River ships use the local Aljmaš berth, placing passengers close to the compact village. There is no large cruise terminal, and the central sights are generally reached on foot. The exact gangway location can vary with river conditions, so follow the ship's directions when going ashore.

Do not depend on finding taxis at the berth. Arrange transport through the ship or in advance for any trip beyond the village. Public transport is not practical for a short port call.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Explore Aljmaš on Foot

Allow 1.5–2.5 hours for the village's main sights. The centerpiece is the modern Church and Sanctuary of Our Lady of Refuge, often called the Danube Swan because of its distinctive shape. When accessible, its memorial collection provides useful context about the destruction and rebuilding of the sanctuary.

Continue along the quiet riverside and through the neighboring streets for views across the Danube. Aljmaš is small, so this option is easy to manage independently without filling the entire port call.

Climb the Stations of the Cross

A hillside path follows 14 carved Stations of the Cross for approximately 500 m (0.3 mi), ending near a large statue and an elevated viewpoint. The climb adds about 45–75 minutes to a village walk. Expect an uphill surface and wear shoes with good grip; it may not suit passengers with limited mobility.

Visit Erdut and Its Wine Country

The Erdut peninsula combines vineyards, Danube viewpoints, wineries and the remains of a medieval tower above the river. Some wineries accept visitors only by prior arrangement, especially outside weekday hours, so this is best booked as a guided outing or prearranged taxi tour. Allow about 3–4 hours, including transport and a tasting.

Wine tastings should never be assumed to accept walk-in visitors. Confirm arrangements before leaving Aljmaš.

Discover Osijek

Osijek lies approximately 26 km (16.2 mi) west of Aljmaš. Its principal visitor area includes the Baroque Tvrđa quarter, Holy Trinity Square and the long Drava riverfront promenade. Allow roughly 4–5 hours for the transfer and a focused city visit.

Independent travel is possible with transport reserved in advance, but a ship excursion is simpler because local taxis and return connections cannot be assumed.

Explore Kopački Rit Nature Park

This extensive wetland near the Drava–Danube confluence is known for birdlife, waterways and floodplain scenery. Visits can combine the visitor center, the White Water-Lily boardwalk and a scheduled boat experience.

Organized excursion recommended. The park is outside Aljmaš, its activities operate to set schedules, and reservations are required for visitor programs. Allow at least half a day and check which experiences are included in the tour.

Self-Guided Village Walk

Riverfront, Sanctuary and Calvary

Suggested route: river berth – Aljmaš waterfront – Church of Our Lady of Refuge – village center – Stations of the Cross – viewpoint – return through the village to the ship.

  • Approximate distance: 2–3 km (1.2–1.9 mi), depending on the berth and how far you continue along the waterfront.
  • Pure walking time: about 40–60 minutes.
  • Recommended total time: 1.5–2.5 hours with church, memorial and viewpoint stops.
  • Difficulty: easy within the village; moderate if the uphill Calvary path is included.
  • Return: retrace the village streets to the river berth, allowing extra time if another tour group is using the gangway.

Passengers wanting a gentler route can omit the Calvary and remain around the church and riverfront.

Nature and River Experiences

The meeting of the Drava and Danube is a notable local landscape, but it should not be treated as a simple walk from the berth. River channels, seasonal water levels and access conditions make a prearranged boat trip or guided excursion the practical choice.

The surrounding forest and vineyard trails can involve slopes, uneven ground and longer distances. Attempt them only with reliable route information and enough time to return; they are better suited to a dedicated guided activity than an improvised port walk.

Practical Tips

  • Carry some water and wear comfortable footwear; shade can be limited along exposed riverfront and hillside sections.
  • Expect fewer shops, taxis and visitor services than at a city cruise port.
  • Church access may be restricted during services, pilgrimages or private events.
  • Aljmaš becomes particularly busy around the Assumption pilgrimage on August 15.
  • Allow a sensible return margin for road excursions and follow the ship's stated all-aboard time.
